reference.title: Scenario 1 — Clearly defined problem, cause and remedy
reference.shortdesc: Consider an HTML document containing a troubleshooting section with a clearly defined problem, its cause,

section.p: Consider an HTML document containing a troubleshooting section with a clearly defined problem, its cause, and the corresponding remedy. The following example shows how the converter transforms this structure into a DITA <troubleshooting> topic.

entry.codeblock:
The Printer Does Not Power On

Cause: The power cable is disconnected.

Remedy:

  1. Connect the power cable securely.
  2. Press the power button.

The Printer Does Not Power On Condition

The printer does not power on.

 Cause

The power cable is disconnected.

 Remedy Connect the power cable securely. Press the power button.

section.p: Result: The heading "The Printer Does Not Power On" states a problem, and the body uses Cause: and Remedy: labels triggering a Troubleshooting topic. The heading text becomes the , since it states the observable problem. The cause text maps to , and the numbered remedy steps map to . The cause and remedy are wrapped together in a single .
